source.title: Generalization Ability of Wide Residual Networks
source.authors: Jian-Fa Lai; Zixiong Yu; Songtao Tian; Qian Lin

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes generalization across training time for wide residual networks, using kernel theory and experiments rather than testing the model-size, sample-size, or double-descent sweeps in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical excess-risk results for early stopping and training to overfit, plus testing-accuracy experiments over training time. Double-descent findings mentioned only through cited work are not recorded as results. The experiment figures are referenced, but their numerical values are not present in the text.
record.test_reason: The study analyses early stopping versus training to interpolation for wide ResNets in the NTK regime. Its experiments compare t_label with t_opt under label corruption. It never measures or describes a fall-rise-fall test-error curve over model size, epochs or samples. Nakkiran et al. is cited only as an example of benign overfitting. The theory concerns the rate at a stopping time and the inconsistency of the interpolation limit, not the double-descent shape. The text does not describe the Figure 1–2 accuracy curves as having a second descent.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors prove uniform RNK→RNTK convergence, a minimax rate for early-stopped wide ResNets, and poor generalization when trained to overfit. Experiments show benign overfitting (t_label near t_opt) with strong signal, but not as label corruption increases. Signal strength is operationalized as the corruption ratio p.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses RNTK/kernel-regression analysis and training-time experiments on residual networks; it does not reproduce double-descent sweeps over model size or sample size.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported timing gap between t_label and t_opt increases as label corruption increases; the synthetic-data experiments use both square and cross-entropy loss.

fits_no_version.finding: In the NTK (lazy) regime, theory says wide ResNets reach the minimax rate when early-stopped and generalize poorly at the interpolation limit (Thms 4.1, 4.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For infinitely wide ResNets under gradient flow, risk over training time is optimized at an intermediate stopping time, and interpolation is not benign.

fits_no_version.finding: The gap between t_label and t_opt grows with label corruption p on synthetic data (both losses) and on CIFAR-10. At p=0 the gap is described as extremely small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign overfitting at t_label depends on signal strength. With more label noise, the zero-label-error time drifts away from the optimal stopping time.

record.problems: The paper's experiments are described through figures, without numerical test-accuracy values in the supplied text. The text reports error bars from 10 replicate experiments for the synthetic timing-gap results, but does not provide a full test-error trajectory or establish a second descent. The theoretical generalization claims rely on the stated RKHS assumption and sufficiently large width.

untested.parts: No reported epoch-wise test-error shape and no second descent described. Only the stopping-time gap is reported.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
Label corruption is varied, but its effect on a double-descent peak or on regularization is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' is downgraded. The paper is about early stopping and benign overfitting, not double descent. No version receives a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve over model size.
The study examines generalization at selected training times and shows test-accuracy figures, but does not establish a full fall-rise-fall curve or a second descent.
No sweep of training sample size near an interpolation threshold.
No comparison of double-descent curves across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations across axes.
Label corruption is varied, but the study does not test whether noise drives a double-descent peak, whether peaks split, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes a peak.
No alternative parameter-count measure or U-shaped reparameterization is tested.

rows.subject: wide residual network
rows.operation_detail: Train with gradient flow and stop at t* proportional to n^(d/(2d−1)).

conditions.value: f* belongs to the RNTK RKHS and has RKHS norm at most R

rows.measure: Excess risk at the early-stopping time
rows.note: Establishes a generalization bound at an early stopping time, not the full error trajectory or a double-descent shape.
rows.check: A theoretical minimax bound at an early-stopping time. It is not a measurement of test error across epochs, so it does not bear on V2's curve shape.

rows.subject: wide residual network
rows.size_stated: width m and sample size n sufficiently large; L ≥ 2
rows.operation_detail: Train until the limit of large training time, when the network nearly fits the data.
rows.measure: Excess risk conditional on the training inputs
rows.value: E[lim inf(t→∞) E(ftm) | X] ≥ c n^(−ε)
rows.note: The result says overfitted networks may generalize poorly; it does not specify the intervening or later test-error trajectory.
rows.check: A theoretical lower bound on excess risk at the t→∞ interpolation limit. It concerns benign versus harmful overfitting, not a peak followed by a second descent.

relation.reason: Section 5 cites Nakkiran et al. [29] for reported benign overfitting, without testing or using its double-descent finding.

tranche.reason: The results concern early-stopping risk bounds, interpolation-limit risk and corruption-dependent stopping-time gaps. They neither establish nor refute a double-descent curve or its proposed mechanisms.

source_check.notes: Figure 1 reports timing-gap means and standard deviations over 10 replicates, omitted from the rows' uncertainty fields; synthetic test labels are also corrupted. Theorem 4.2 does not establish inconsistency; the CIFAR-10 setup contains an apparent model-name typo.
